caveat: The privileged container was required because this Docker kernel denied unprivileged user namespaces. This validates the bubblewrap configuration, not the container's own containment. A production deployment must run the worker on a host or microVM where unprivileged user namespaces (or a rootless container runtime with the required namespaces) are enabled, and must not rely on --privileged.
findings: The worker applies its own seccomp filter inside the sandbox after bwrap setup: the command reports Seccomp: 2 and unshare/mount return EPERM. The container's inherited seccomp is disabled, so the inner filter is the effective one.

cgroup v2 pids.max and memory.max enforced the fork and memory bounds. In the full probe sequence the fork bomb was stopped by the wall clock; an isolated direct test with the seccomp wrapper stopped it in 0.84s with BlockingIOError. The bound is enforced either way; the quick-EAGAIN path is proven in isolation.
The host cgroup hierarchy had to be mounted read-write; the default container cgroup fs is read-only and the worker fails closed without a writable cgroup v2 leaf.
/etc is a tmpfs with individual read-only file binds and a read-only remount. A plain --dir /etc left the directory writable and failed the write-escape probe.
The probe does not test microVM isolation.
